t: Aurangzeb appoints Shaista Khan subedar of Bengal
c: In 1664, Aurangzeb appointed Shaista Khan the subedar (governor) of Bengal.

t: Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh trade with Aceh
c: Aurangzeb, and his brother, Dara Shikoh, participated with Aceh trade and Aurangzeb himself also exchanging presents with the Sultan of Aceh in 1641.

t: Subhan Quli Khan recognizes Aurangzeb

t: Abbas II of Persia sends embassy to Mughal court
c: Abbas II of Persia sent an embassy in 1661.

t: Ethiopian Emperor Fasilides sends embassy to Aurangzeb
c: Ethiopian Emperor Fasilides dispatched an embassy to India in 1664–65 to congratulate Aurangzeb upon his accession to the throne of the Mughal Empire.

t: Jat peasants of Bharatpur rebel and are defeated
c: In 1669, the Hindu Jat peasants of Bharatpur around Mathura rebelled but were defeated.

t: Sambhaji captured and executed by Aurangzeb
c: In 1689, Aurangzeb's armies captured Shivaji's son Sambhaji and executed him.

t: Raja Ram Jat captured and beheaded
c: On 4 July 1688, Raja Ram Jat was captured and beheaded.

t: Aurangzeb sends Shaista Khan to recover Maratha forts
c: In 1659, Aurangzeb sent his trusted general and maternal uncle Shaista Khan, the wali in Golconda to recover forts lost to the Maratha rebels.

t: Mir Jumla II ordered to recover lost territories
c: In 1660 Mir Jumla II, the viceroy of Bengal, was ordered to recover the lost territories.

t: Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib built in Delhi
c: In 1789, Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib was built in Delhi at the place where Guru Tegh Bahadur was beheaded.

t: Guru Gobind Singh sends Zafarnamah letter
c: In 1705, Guru Gobind Singh sent a letter entitled Zafarnamah, which accused Aurangzeb of cruelty and betraying Islam.

t: Khalsa formation leads to Sikh Confederacy
c: Guru Gobind Singh's formation of Khalsa in 1699 led to the establishment of the Sikh Confederacy and later Sikh Empire.

c: In 1497, he besieged Samarkand for seven months before eventually gaining control over it.

t: Ismail I defeats and kills Shaybani Khan
c: Meanwhile, Shaybani was defeated and killed by Ismail I, Shah of Shi'a Safavid Persia, in 1510.

t: Babur takes control of Badakhshan
c: In 1521, he took control of Badakhshan after the death of Uways Mirza.

t: Babur annexes Kandahar from Arghun dynasty
c: In 1522, he besieged and annexed Kandahar from the Arghun dynasty.

t: Daulat Khan Lodi driven out by Ibrahim Lodi
c: Babur started for Lahore in 1524 but found that Daulat Khan Lodi had been driven out by forces sent by Ibrahim Lodi.

t: Babur reaches Panipat facing Ibrahim Lodi
c: He reached Panipat on 20 April 1526 and there met Ibrahim Lodi's numerically superior army of about 100,000 soldiers and 1,000 elephants.

t: Babur offers peace terms to Medini Rai
c: Upon reaching Chanderi, on 20 January 1528, Babur offered Shamsabad to Medini Rai in exchange for Chanderi as a peace overture, but the offer was rejected.

t: Babur writes secret will to Humayun

t: Jahangir succeeds Akbar as Mughal emperor
c: Following Akbar's death, Jahangir succeeded him on 3 November 1605.

t: Jahangir marries Bhati Rajput princess
c: Another wife was a Bhati Rajput princess daughter of Rawal Bhim Singh of Jaisalmer, whom Jahangir married in 1587.

t: Saliha Banu Begum designated Padshah Begum
c: After the death of Saliha Banu Begum in 1620, she was designated the title of Padshah Begum and held it until the death of Jahangir in 1627.

t: Khusrau blinded and imprisoned
c: After rebelling and being defeated again for the second time, Khusrau was then blinded and imprisoned until 1619.

t: Khusrau sent on mission to Deccan
c: In 1620, Khusrau was sent on a mission to Deccan with his brother, Shah Jahan.

t: Islam Khan subdues rebel Musa Khan in Bengal
c: In 1608, Jahangir posted Islam Khan I to subdue the rebel Musa Khan, the Masnad-e-Ala of the Baro-Bhuyan confederacy in Bengal, who was able to imprison him.

t: Thomas Roe arrives as British ambassador
c: In 1614, The East India Company persuaded King James I to send a British ambassador to the Mughal court, Thomas Roe.

t: Jahangir captures Kangra Fort
c: In 1615, Jahangir captured Kangra Fort, whose Katoch rulers came under Mughal vassalship during the reign of Akbar.

t: Abbas the Great attacks Kandahar
c: Simultaneously, the Safavid emperor Abbas the Great attacked Kandahar in the winter of 1622.

t: Civil war ends between Mahabat Khan and Khurram
c: After a series of victories by Mahabat Khan over Khurram, the civil war finally ended in October 1625.

t: Gujarat Sultan plans assault on Mughal territories
c: In 1535 Humayun was made aware that the Sultan of Gujarat was planning an assault on the Mughal territories in Bayana with Portuguese aid.

t: Bahadur Shah recaptures Gujarat in revolt
c: In a popular revolt Bahadur Shah recaptured all of Gujarat in 1536 and began an attack on Malwa.

t: Bairam Khan joins Humayun for Indian campaign
c: By 1554, Bairam Khan left Kandahar to join Humayun as he prepared for an Indian campaign.

t: Title mansa adopted for Mali emperors
Neighboring states chip away at Mali's borders
c: However, from 1507 onwards neighboring states such as Diarra, Great Fulo, Yatenga, and the Songhai Empire chipped away at Mali's borders.

t: Soumaoro Kanté conquers Manden territory
c: In 1203, the Sosso king and sorcerer Soumaoro Kanté came to power and reportedly conquered much of Manden.

t: Mansa Musa annexes Timbuktu

t: Songhai Empire conquers Mema
c: The rising Songhai Empire conquered Mema, one of Mali's oldest possessions, in 1465.

t: Sunni Ali captures Timbuktu from Tuareg
c: It then seized Timbuktu from the Tuareg in 1468 under Sunni Ali Ber.

t: Naba Nasséré conquers Macina and Wagadou
c: In 1477, the Mossi emperor Naba Nasséré made yet another raid into Macina, this time conquering it and the old province of BaGhana (Wagadou).

t: Mansa Mahmud II establishes relations with Portugal
c: In an attempt to stem the tide, Mansa Mahmud Keita II opened diplomatic relations with Portugal, receiving the envoys Pêro d'Évora and Gonçalo Enes in 1487.

t: Askia Muhammad defeats Mali general Fati Quali Keita
c: Songhai forces under the command of Askia Muhammad I defeated the Mali general Fati Quali Keita in 1502 and seized the province of Diafunu.

t: Mali reasserts authority over Bendugu and Kala
c: Songhai authority over Bendugu and Kala declined by 1571, and Mali may have been able to reassert some authority over them.

t: Mali reasserts authority over former Gambian subjects
c: The breakup of the Wolof Empire allowed Mali to reassert authority over some of its former subjects on the north bank of the Gambia, such as Wuli, by 1576.

t: Mali Empire collapses
c: The Gbara or Great Assembly would serve as the Mandinka deliberative body and council of state until the collapse of the empire in 1645.

t: Maghan Keita I succeeds Mansa Musa
c: Mansa Musa Keita was succeeded by his son, Maghan Keita I, in 1337.

t: Souleyman Keita succeeds to Mali throne
c: But the Mali Empire built by his predecessors was too strong for even his misrule and it passed intact to Musa's brother, Souleyman Keita in 1341.

t: Maghan Keita II crowned Mansa

t: Mahmud Keita becomes Maghan Keita III
c: He reigned less than a year before Mahmud Keita, descendant of Mansa Gao, rebelled and killed him, taking the throne as Mansa Maghan Keita III in 1390.

t: Tuareg capture Timbuktu and Oualata
c: Timbuktu and Oualata fell to the Tuareg, led by Akil Ag-Amalwal, in 1433.

t: Sunni Ali captures Timbuktu and Djenne
c: Sunni Ali conquered Timbuktu from the Tuareg in 1469 and then, after a long siege, took Djenne in 1471.

t: Tenguella invades Kingdom of Diarra
c: In 1511, Tenguella invaded the Kingdom of Diarra, whose rulers called for help from the Songhai.

t: Umar Komajago kills Tenguella, Songhai takes control
c: Umar Komajago, a brother of Askia Mohammad I, answered the call, killing the invader in 1512 and establishing Songhai hegemony in the area.

t: Jolof Empire falls after Battle of Danki
c: The Jolof Empire, under pressure from the Denianke for decades, finally fell apart after the 1549 Battle of Danki.

t: Death of Mansa Djata
c: Mansa Djata died in around 1255, and he was succeeded by his son who ruled until 1270.

t: Mansa Ouati rules Mali
c: Mansa Ouati, an adopted son of Mansa Djata, ruled from 1270 to 1274.

t: Khalifa succeeds Mansa Ouati
c: Mansa Ouati died in 1274, and Khalifa promptly marched in to take the throne.

t: Sakura usurps Mansa Abubakari I
c: Mansa Abubakari I was usurped by general and former slave Sakura or Sabakura in 1285.

t: Mali Empire stretches to Kanem border
c: By the time of his murder in 1300, the Mali Empire already stretched from the Atlantic to the border of the Kanem Empire.

t: Mansa Musa I comes to power
c: In 1312, Mansa Musa I came to power and brought the empire even more fame and prestige with his legendary Hajj to Mecca.

t: Mansa Suleyman dies and is succeeded
c: Mansa Suleyman died in 1360 and was succeeded by his son, Camba, who was quickly overthrown by a son of Maghan I.

t: Mansa Musa II becomes Mali ruler
c: The throne officially went to Mansa Musa II in 1374, son of Mansa Mari Djata II.

t: Maghan II succeeds Musa II
c: Musa II was succeeded by his brother, Maghan II, in 1387.

t: Portugal sends envoy to Mali
c: The defeats forced Portugal's king to dispatch his courtier Diogo Gomes in 1456 to secure peace.

t: Mansa Mahmud II succeeds Mansa Uli II
c: Mansa Uli II was succeeded by Mansa Mahmud II in 1481.

t: Tengela leads Fulbe from Futa Jallon against Mali
c: In 1490, Tengela led the Fulbe out of Futa Jallon forcing the Malian forces to retreat to the Gambia.

t: Askia Muhammad dismantles Mali's remaining provinces
c: From 1500 to 1510, Askia Muhammad's forces picked apart Mali's remaining provinces in the Sahel.

t: Askia Muhammad raids Galam, ending Mali rule
c: In 1506, Askia Muhammad raids Galam on the Senegal river, wiping away the last vestiges of Mali's rule in the Sahel.

t: Askiya Isma'il ends peaceful Songhai-Mali relations
c: The accession of Askiya Isma’il in 1537, marked the end of peaceable relations between Songhay and Mali.

t: Mansa Mahmud III flees Niani as Dawud attacks
c: Finally in 1545, Mansa Mahmud III was forced to flee the capital of Niani as Kurminafari (and later Askia) Dawud sacked the city.

t: Mansa Mahmud III conquers Begho
c: In 1550 Mahmud III sent a cavalry force to conquer Begho in response to its repusal to pay the tribute that he requested.

t: Askiya Dawud raids Malian town Suma
c: In 1558, Askiya Dawud launched a raid on the Malian town of Suma.

t: Nakbe established as earliest Maya city
c: Nakbe in the Petén department of Guatemala is the earliest well-documented city in the Maya lowlands, where large structures have been dated to around 750 BC.
